content: For context, in 2024, South Africa successfully produced approximately 3.3 million tonnes of ferrochrome, which constituted a substantial portion of the global production total of 17.5 million tonnes, underscoring its dominance in the sector at that time [Source 3]. However, the operational landscape for mid-tier chrome mining companies is increasingly complex, shaped by a confluence of evolving national policies, infrastructural constraints, and shifting international demand. The strategic pivot toward raw ore exports is clearly reflected in recent trade data and logistical trends. As of January 2026, there has been a notable increase in South Africa's chrome ore exports routed through neighboring Mozambique [Source 4]. Specifically, 399,038.65 metric tonnes of chrome ore were exported via this corridor during January 2026, representing a marked increase compared to the 284,572.28 metric tonnes exported in January 2025, though slightly lower than the 413,899.98 metric tonnes recorded in December 2025 [Source 4]. The dominance of Tharisa plc is underpinned by its proactive operational advancements and strategic capacity expansions. A notable industry-specific advancement reflecting this proactive stance is Tharisa's successful initiation of its first underground blast at the Tharisa Mine prior to February 2026 [Source 2]. Although this milestone represents the progress of a single corporate entity rather than a sector-wide trend, it exemplifies the operational strategies required to maintain a leading market share in the highly competitive mid-tier segment [Source 2]. By transitioning to or integrating underground operations, companies like Tharisa aim to extend mine life and access deeper, higher-grade ore bodies, thereby securing their supply lines for both domestic obligations and lucrative international export markets. The operational strategies and market positioning of these mid-tier companies must also be contextualized within broader global market projections. The global market size for chrome in 2026 was estimated at 5.15 billion, a valuation heavily supported by South Africa's significant supply contributions [Source 1]. Furthermore, specific segments of the downstream market indicate sustained demand that will continue to pull raw materials from South African mid-tier producers.
